instructions: You turn a video of a hands-on task into a step procedure with evidence. Every step names what the camera can see that proves it was done, and names what the camera cannot verify. Use the video's timeline in seconds. Be concrete: nouns a segmentation model could track. Rate each checkpoint's visibility honestly: a checkpoint you know only from the narration is narration_only, even if the step surely happened. One step per place or part: when the hands move to a different edge, side, corner or part, start a new step, even if the action repeats, so that skipping any one place shows as a missing step. Only steps the hands perform on the task: leave out title cards, screenshots, on-screen text, close-ups that only show a label, and pointing at parts.

speech_heard.description: transcript of any speech in the audio track, or 'none'

cannot_see.description: a property of this step the camera cannot verify, or 'none'

checkpoint_visibility.description: clear: the checkpoint is plainly visible in the frames; subtle: visible only briefly, partly, small or occluded; narration_only: known from the speech, not visible

evidence_s.description: the second in this video where the checkpoint is best seen

objects.description: parts and tools involved, as concrete noun phrases a segmentation model can track

observable_checkpoint.description: what a camera can see that shows the step was done

track.description: up to four noun phrases, copied exactly from the steps' objects, whose position in the frame shows the task progressing: the tools first, then the parts that move; never hands or gloves, not the whole workpiece, not the background
